title: One reviewer's round-one findings
description: What a single specialist returns after reading the design document once, through one lens, with no knowledge of what the other reviewers found. The id pattern is tightened per reviewer at call time — the orchestrator injects the reviewer's own slug — so a finding can always be traced back to the agent that raised it, and no reviewer can file a finding under another's name.

agent.description: The reviewer's slug, matching its charter filename.

lens.description: One or two sentences stating what this reviewer judged and what it deliberately left to others. Written by the reviewer, so a reader can tell whether a finding was in scope.

id.description: <reviewer-slug>-F<n>, numbered from 1. Stable: the cross-examination round and the synthesis both cite it, and a finding whose id moves between rounds cannot be traced.

title.description: One line naming the problem, not the topic. 'The satellite may be unlandable at full upgrades', not 'The endgame'.

severity.description: BLOCKING: the design cannot be built or cannot be finished as written. MAJOR: it ships worse, or a decision has to be made before code is written. MINOR: worth fixing, costs nothing to defer.

problem.description: What is wrong, argued rather than asserted. A finding that does not survive being read by somebody who disagrees is not a finding.

where.description: Where in the document this comes from: section numbers, headings or quoted phrases. At least one, and they must be real — an unlocatable finding cannot be checked and will be contested for that alone.

why_it_matters.description: The consequence if nothing changes. Concrete: what the player hits, or what the build runs out of.

proposed_fix.description: Optional, and deliberately not required. A reviewer who can only describe a problem has still done the job; one that invents a fix to look useful has made the moderator's work harder.

out_of_scope.description: Things this reviewer noticed and is deliberately not filing, because they belong to another lens. Useful to the moderator: it shows where two reviewers were looking at the same passage.
